---
title: "Iterative Problem-Solving and Decision-Making"
date: "2026-4-30"
image: slides/AppImage.png
---

Throughout the development of my fitness tracking application, I consistently revised both the design and functionality based on 
testing and usability concerns. One major decision was simplifying the app’s focus from wearable integration to user-entered 
workout data. This change made the application more accessible and allowed me to focus on creating meaningful workout evaluations 
and progress analysis rather than relying on external hardware APIs. I also iteratively redesigned the chart system several times 
to improve readability and better visualize workout trends. These revisions demonstrated how software development is an ongoing 
problem-solving process where user experience, technical limitations, and project scope all influence final design decisions.

Another important aspect of the iterative process was incorporating feedback from presentations, testing sessions, and personal 
evaluation of the app’s usability. As I continued developing the project, I realized that clarity and simplicity were just as 
important as adding new features. For example, I adjusted navigation layouts, improved the organization of workout data, and 
refined the visual styling to create a more professional and intuitive interface. These repeated improvements helped me better 
understand how developers must continuously adapt their solutions rather than expecting the first implementation to be perfect.
